title: Glossary
markdown:
Every term from the course, in alphabetical order. The lesson that introduces each one is in brackets.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **ABI** | Application binary interface: the rules compiled code follows to work together, such as type sizes, struct layout, calling conventions and name decoration. A DLL's interface is a promise about its ABI. (3.01) |
| **AddRef / Release** | The two reference-counting methods of a COM-style interface. AddRef takes a reference; Release drops one and deletes the object at zero. (3.04) |
| **API set** | A name such as `api-ms-win-core-file-l1-1-0.dll` that Windows redirects to a real system DLL without any search. (1.06) |
| **ASLR** | Address space layout randomisation: Windows loads modules at random addresses to make attacks harder, so relocation is normal. (1.02) |
| **Binary compatibility** | Programs already compiled against one version of a DLL keep working with a newer one without being rebuilt. (3.01) |
| **Calling convention** | The agreement about where arguments go, where the result comes back and who cleans up the stack. x64 Windows has one; 32-bit Windows has several. (2.02) |
| **Capability** | A named feature of a plugin contract with its own version, which a plugin can require. (5.02) |
| **CRT** | The C runtime library: `malloc`, `new`, `printf` and friends. A module gets it shared (`/MD`) or private (`/MT`). (2.05) |
| **Decorated (mangled) name** | The symbol name a C++ compiler gives a function, encoding its scope and types so that overloads differ, such as `?add@@YAHHH@Z`. (2.01) |
| **.def file** | A module-definition file that lists a DLL's exports by hand, with optional ordinals, `NONAME` and `DATA`. (1.04) |
| **Delay loading** | Linking against a DLL's import library but loading it only when one of its functions is first called. (4.03) |
| **DLL** | Dynamic-link library: compiled code and data in a separate PE file that a process maps and calls into. (1.01) |
| **DLL Hell** | Programs breaking because an installer replaced a shared DLL with an incompatible version of the same name. (3.05) |
| **DLL planting** | Placing a file with a DLL's name where the search order finds it before the real one. Also called search-order hijacking. (4.02) |
| **DllMain** | A DLL's optional entry point, called when the DLL is attached to or detached from a process and when threads start and end. (2.04) |
| **dllexport / dllimport** | `__declspec` attributes that put a symbol in a DLL's export table, and tell the compiler a symbol comes from a DLL. (1.03) |
| **Exception barrier** | A try/catch around the body of an exported function that turns every exception into an error code. (2.06) |
| **Export table** | The part of a PE file listing the names, ordinals and RVAs of what a module offers to others. (1.01) |
| **extern "C"** | C linkage: no name decoration and no overloading, so the exported name is plain. (2.01) |
| **FreeLibrary** | Drops one reference to a loaded DLL; at zero the DLL is unmapped. (2.03) |
| **Function table** | A versioned struct of function pointers returned by one exported function, used as an interface. (3.03) |
| **GetProcAddress** | Returns the address of a DLL's exported function by name or ordinal. (2.03) |
| **Header-only library** | Reusable code entirely in headers, compiled into every program that includes it. (4.05) |
| **Host** | The program that loads plugins or a hot-reloaded DLL and calls into them. (5.01) |
| **Hot reload** | Replacing a running program's code (a DLL) with a rebuilt version without restarting or losing state. (5.03) |
| **Import address table (IAT)** | A module's array of slots, one per imported function, filled by the loader with real addresses. (1.05) |
| **Import library** | A small `.lib` that tells the linker which DLL each function comes from, without containing their code. (1.05) |
| **Known DLLs** | Core system DLLs that Windows always loads from System32, whatever the search order says. (4.01) |
| **Loader** | The part of Windows (in `ntdll.dll`) that maps modules into a process, resolves imports and runs initialisation. (1.02) |
| **Loader lock** | A process-wide lock held while modules are loaded and unloaded; DllMain and global constructors run under it. (2.04) |
| **LoadLibraryW / LoadLibraryExW** | Map a DLL into the process at run time, the second with flags that control the search. (2.03, 4.02) |
| **Opaque handle** | A pointer to a type that is declared but never defined for callers, so its contents can change between versions. (3.01) |
| **Ordinal** | A DLL export's number. Exports can be found by ordinal instead of name. (1.04) |
| **PE file** | Portable Executable: the file format of Windows executables and DLLs. (1.01) |
| **Plugin** | A DLL the host finds and loads at run time through a fixed contract, which it was not built with. (5.01) |
| **QueryInterface** | The COM-style method that asks an object for another interface it supports. (3.04) |
| **Reference count** | A count of holders. DLLs are counted by LoadLibrary and FreeLibrary; COM-style objects by AddRef and Release. (2.03, 3.04) |
| **Relocation** | Fixing stored absolute addresses when a module is loaded away from its preferred base. (1.02) |
| **RVA** | Relative virtual address: an offset from the start of a loaded module. (1.02) |
| **Safe DLL search mode** | The setting, on by default, that searches the current directory after the system folders. (4.01) |
| **Search order** | The list of places Windows tries when a DLL is requested by name only. (4.01) |
| **Semantic versioning** | MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH: major for breaking changes, minor for additions, patch for fixes. (3.05) |
| **SetDefaultDllDirectories** | Restricts every later name-only load in the process to safe folders. (4.02) |
| **Static library** | A `.lib` whose code the linker copies into the executable. (1.01) |
| **Thunk** | A small piece of code that stands in for a function, such as the delay-load stub that loads the DLL on the first call. (4.03) |
| **Version resource** | Version information compiled into a PE file, shown in Explorer's Details tab. (4.04) |
| **Versioned struct** | A struct whose first member is its own size, so a library can tell which version the caller sent. (3.03) |
| **vtable / vptr** | The table of a class's virtual function pointers, and the hidden pointer to it at the start of each object. (3.04) |
